proposals: The Department of Food and Public Distribution should publish central-pool stocks against the buffer norm as a monthly downloadable series on a fixed release date, so figures like the 476.85 LMT against 214.1 LMT on 1 January 2025 can be kept current instead of going stale for more than a year.

The Department of Food and Public Distribution should publish state-wise procurement for each marketing season within three months of its close, so a state's share of the pool, such as Punjab's roughly 47 per cent of wheat, is not available only for a season that is already two cycles old.

FCI and the Department of Food and Public Distribution should report rice procurement in every release in both paddy and rice-equivalent terms, stating the out-turn ratio applied, so the 832.17 LMT paddy figure and the 544.8 LMT rice figure can be reconciled without guesswork.

FCI should publish its annual storage cost per tonne for each channel — owned godowns, CWC, hired SWC space, PEG and other hired capacity — together with the cost of holding stock above the buffer norm, so the price of a 262.75 LMT surplus held mostly in leased space is visible.
